note: d107. Older questions offer 'turn on default encryption' as the answer to 'make sure new objects are encrypted at rest'; it is now automatic. fr-0043 (requests-21): `changed` set from the default encryption FAQ sentences on existing unencrypted buckets and 'no longer disable'.

changed.was: no base level of encryption: existing unencrypted buckets (no default encryption configured) did not encrypt new object uploads, and encryption of new uploads could be disabled

evidence.quote: Starting January 5, 2023, all new object uploads to Amazon S3 are automatically encrypted at no additional cost and with no impact on performance.
SSE-S3, which uses 256-bit Advanced Encryption Standard (AES-256), is automatically applied to all new buckets and to any existing S3 bucket that doesn't already have default encryption configured.

Amazon S3 now configures default encryption on all existing unencrypted buckets to apply server-side encryption with S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) as the base level of encryption for new objects uploaded to these buckets.
You can no longer disable encryption for new object uploads.
